chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who prays over two dead bodies or three dead bodies, how should he pray over them?

He (peace be upon him) said: 'If there were three, or two, or ten, or more than that, let him pray over them one prayer, exclaiming five Takbeers over them just as he prays over one deceased, and he has prayed over them all.'

He places one deceased, then places the other parallel to the first, then places the head of the third parallel to the rear of the second, like a staircase, until he finishes with all of them, whatever their number. So when he has arranged them thus, he stands in the middle and exclaims five Takbeers, doing as he does when he prays over one deceased.

He was asked: 'What if the deceased were men and women?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should begin with the men, placing the head of the second parallel to the rear of the first, until he finishes with all the men. Then he places the head of the woman parallel to the rear of the last man, then places the head of the other woman parallel to the rear of the first woman, until he finishes with all of them.'
So when he has arranged them thus, he stands in the middle, in the middle of the men, and exclaims Takbeers and prays over them just as he prays over one deceased.

And he was asked about a deceased who had been prayed over, and when the Imam concluded, the deceased was found upside down, his feet in the place of his head. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should be straightened and the prayer is repeated over him, even if he had been carried, as long as he had not been buried. If he had been buried, the prayer has passed; he is not prayed over while he is buried.'
ai.seo_question: How should one perform the funeral prayer (Salat al-Janazah) for multiple deceased individuals according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the Shia jurisprudence for praying over multiple deceased individuals, establishing that a single prayer with five Takbeers suffices for any number of bodies arranged in a staircase formation. It further specifies the protocol for mixed-gender groups, prioritizing men before women, and clarifies that if a body is found inverted after the Imam's Salam, the prayer is repeated unless the body has already been buried, in which case the prayer is deemed complete. This ruling underscores the flexibility and completeness of the Janazah prayer in Shia tradition, emphasizing the validity of the act over the precise orientation of the body post-prayer.
